# 1) Diagnostics and transformations:

### A) Model_M = IB ~ Stressor:

I am going to choose the larger subset since all subsets have the same stressors and IBs:

#### CRP:

The largest subset for CRP mediations is *df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final*

```{r}
# List of stressors: 
stressors= c("s_phys_abus_CAT", "s_psy_abus_CAT", "s_phys_abus", "s_sex_mol", "s_sex_mol", "s_felt_loved", "s_felt_hated", "s_neglect", "s_loneliness")

#### 1) Diagnostics using original data:

# Set output directory for plots
dir.create("../outs/Diagnostics", showWarnings = FALSE)

pdf("../outs/Diagnostics/Diagnostics_CRP_stress_lm.pdf", width = 10, height = 5)

for (stress in stressors){
  # Define the model: IB ~ stress: 
    model <- glm(as.formula(paste("CRP ~", stress, "+ sex + age + bmi + SES + phys_act + depression")), 
                 family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
                 data= df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final)
    
    # Plot diagnostic plots for residuals:
    # Save plots to PDF only (no console output)
    par(mfrow = c(2,3))  # Arrange 2x2 plots per page
    invisible(capture.output({
    plot(model, main = paste("Model: CRP ~", stress))
    hist(residuals(model), main = paste("Model: CRP ~", stress))
    }))
}

dev.off()
```
The residuals are skewed and non-homogenuosly distributed --> I will transform CRP (IN ALL 3 SUBSETS):


```{r}
#### 2) Apply inverse-normal transformation to CRP in all 3 datasets:
cat("Before transformation: ", summary(df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final$CRP), "\n")

# Apply inverse normal transformation to CRP variable for each dataset

df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_2trailm_as_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_2trailm_as_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_2trailm_as_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_3matpat_pal_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_3matpat_pal_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_3matpat_pal_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_4numem_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_4numem_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_4numem_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_5fluidin_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_5fluidin_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_5fluidin_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_6symbds_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_6symbds_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_6symbds_final$CRP)))
df_CRP_7towerre_final$CRP = qnorm((rank(df_CRP_7towerre_final$CRP, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(df_CRP_7towerre_final$CRP)))


cat("After transformation: ", summary(df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final$CRP))
```



```{r}
#### 3) Diagnostics using transformed CRP:

pdf("../outs/Diagnostics/Diagnostics_CRP_stress_lm_transf.pdf", width = 10, height = 5)

for (stress in stressors){
```

#### Other IBs:

TNF and ICAM1 are skewed; ESEL look approximately normal, so I will only transform TNF and ICAM1 (IN ALL 7 SUBSETS):

#### Poisson models:

The CFs: Pairs matching (Immediate Episodic Memory) and Numeric memory (Working Memory) are COUNT data.


```{r}
library(performance) # to conduct overdispersion test

##### 1) Immediate Episodic Memory:

### A) CRP: 
for (stress in stressors){
  model_Y= glm(as.formula(paste("cf_pairs_match_1 ~", stress, "+ CRP + sex + age + bmi + SES + phys_act + depression")),
               family = poisson(link = "log"),
                   data = df_CRP_1pairsm_rt_final)
  
    # Run Overdispersion Test
      overdispersion_result <- check_overdispersion(model_Y)
      
      # Print results
      print(paste("Model: Immediate Episodic Memory ~", stress, "+ CRP"))
      print(overdispersion_result)
}



### B) Other IBs: 
for (stress in stressors){
  for (IB in IBs){
    model_Y= glm(as.formula(paste("cf_pairs_match_1 ~", stress, "+",  IB, " + sex + age + bmi + SES + phys_act + depression")),
                 family = poisson(link = "log"),
                 data = df_IBs_1pairsm_rt_final)
    
    # Run Overdispersion Test
      overdispersion_result <- check_overdispersion(model_Y)
      
      # Print results
      print(paste("Model: Immediate Episodic Memory ~", stress, "+", IB))
      print(overdispersion_result)
  }
}



```

All diagnostics for Immediate Episodic Memory (outcome) using all IBs look fine.
